{"id": "23859900-243d-4b7d-bec7-6f0e4190d7b7", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is the difference between an Application Load Balancer and a Network Load Balancer?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "6d3d759e-2b54-4ef4-a83b-4271469505d2", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "thinking", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "This is a general AWS conceptual question rather than something about the product itself, so the product-knowledge verification rule doesn't apply here\u2014I can just answer directly from stable general knowledge, keeping it concise.\n\n"}]}

{"id": "d2b1333f-8fbf-4c28-9a90-0aee2299a2fc", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Both are Elastic Load Balancing types, but they work at different layers of the network stack.

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query string, HTTP method, source IP | Connection-based: protocol and port |
| **Performance** | Good, with more per-request processing | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes well |
| **IP addressing** | DNS name only. IPs can change. | One static IP per AZ, and you can attach Elastic IPs. It also supports PrivateLink. |
| **Client source IP** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved at the network level, depending on target type |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS with SNI and can authenticate users through OIDC or Cognito | Terminates or passes through TLS |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, ALBs |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported (added in 2023) |
| **Extras** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, WAF integration | Static IPs, PrivateLink endpoint services, long-lived connections |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, microservices, or APIs.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, such as `/api` going to one service and `/web` to another.
- You want to use AWS WAF, Lambda targets, or built-in user authentication.
- You run containers (ECS or EKS) and need flexible routing to many services behind one load balancer.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency, or you expect millions of requests per second.
- You handle non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT/MQTT, or custom TCP/UDP services.
- Clients or firewalls need to allow-list fixed IP addresses.
- You want to expose a service privately to other VPCs or accounts through AWS PrivateLink.

You can also combine them. An NLB placed in front of an ALB gives you static IPs and PrivateLink support, plus the ALB's Layer 7 routing.

If you're deciding for a specific workload in your environment, tell me what it does. I can also look at the load balancers you already have.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
